sources.citation: Adriani, N. 1931. Spraakkunst der Bare'e-taal (Verhandelingen KBG 70). Bandoeng: Nix. par. 4 'Klemtoon', pp. 23-25 (held for pamo1252)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For Bare'e (Pamona, pamo1252), not Tombelala: 'De grondwoorden, die in het B. nooit minder dan twee lettergrepen tellen, hebben den klemtoon op de voorlaatste syllabe'; prefixes never shift stress; -aka and fossil -a(ni)/-o(ni) move it one place rightward; the 'loose' echo-vowel final syllable does not count. Relevant only via Adriani & Kruyt's 1914 identification of Baria as 'the same language as Bare'e'.

sources.citation: Mead, David. n.d. [2013-2016]. 'The Tombelala Language', Sulawesi Language Alliance language page (the Internet Archive 2016-09-14)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; location, classification (Adriani & Kruyt 1914:13 dialect of Pamona; Mead & Mead 1991 separate language), population 1,100 (1989), vitality. Sulang word-list series 001-011 contains no Tombelala list.

sources.citation: Mead, David E. 1999. The Bungku-Tolaki languages of south-eastern Sulawesi, Indonesia (Pacific Linguistics D-91). Canberra: ANU. (held text layer)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tombelala mentioned only pp. 23 and 61-62 (a Pamona community around Lamberea; hule 'heart' borrowed from Bungku; not a Mori language); no Tombelala data or stress remark.

sources.citation: Mead, David & Melanie Mead. 1991. Survey of the Pamona dialects of kecamatan Bungku Tengah. In Timothy Friberg (ed.), UNHAS-SIL: More Sulawesi sociolinguistic surveys, 1987-1991 (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 11), 121-142. Ujung Pandang: SIL. [SIL archives 61262; whole volume downloaded via Internet Archive copy of the sil.org PDF]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 5 'Phonological evidence' (pp. 129-130 = PDF pp. 138-139) covers only Tombelala loss of y between low vowels (raa < raya), the voiceless variant of the bilabial fricative, and loss of m- from verbal prefixes (atu'a < matu'a, elinja < melinja); no word list with transcription is appended; stress/accent never mentioned for Tombelala (the only 'stress' hit in the volume is in the Saluan paper).

sources.citation: Adriani, N. & Alb. C. Kruyt. 1914. De Bare'e-sprekende Toradja's van Midden-Celebes, deel III: Taal- en letterkundige schets der Bare'e-taal en overzicht van het taalgebied Celebes-Zuid-Halmahera. Batavia: Landsdrukkerij. pp. 13-14, 31-32 (Delpher MMKB31:040326000, scans 27-28, 45-46; scanned of scans 20-75 saved, page images of pp. 13, 14, 31 saved)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement for Baria/Tombelala. p.13: the Dore'e-, Baria- and Nde'e-'talen' 'nagenoeg niet verschillen van het Bare'e en moeten beschouwd worden als kolonies der Bare'e-taal'; p.31: 'Het Baria.. is de taal der To Belala.. Hunne taal is dezelfde als het Bare'e en gelijkt het meest op 't Ampanasch dialect (aoende'e)', with heavy Bungku loan vocabulary and ma- > a- on adjectives. Klemtoon remarks in this volume (pp. 23, 25, 33-34) concern Bare'e proper and the Ampana dialect (pretonic syllable reduction), not Baria.
